newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine pension funds managed $6.59 bln in April.
newsitem.headline: Argentine pension funds managed $6.59 bln in April.

text.p: The funds managed by Argentina's private pension system rose to $6.59 billion in April from $5.33 billion at the end of 1996, the Superintendency of Pension and Retirement Funds said Monday.
In April 1996 the funds managed $3.41 billion.

The Superintendency said in a release that, of the funds managed, $3.06 billion, or 46.6 percent, were invested in Argentine government bonds. That compared with $2.56 billion, or 48.1 percent of the total, invested in government bonds at the end of last year.
Stocks accounted for 17.4 percent, or $1.15 billion of funds invested in April, compared with 18.7 percent amounting to $864 million at the end of 1996.
Funds invested in fixed term deposits came to 16.5 percent, or $1.09 billion of the total in April, up from 14.2 percent, or $755 million at the end of last year.
The funds held $99 million in cash at the end of April, up from $97 million at the end of December.
